rubrics.justification: It recognizes a poor-quality blastocyst with indistinct ICM/TE, but it is inconsistent with the provided Gardner 1DD and adds uncertain image-specific claims such as compact ICM, collapse, and no fragmentation/granularity that may not be reliably visible.

It integrates age, low AMH/low oocyte yield, prior IVF failures/miscarriage, tubal factor, BMI, endometrium, and semen parameters into prognosis reasonably well, though some interactions are only loosely developed.

Overall logic is understandable, but there are notable inconsistencies: probability estimates vary (5-10%, 5-8%, 2-5%), embryo morphology is described both as having a compact ICM and as lacking a clear ICM, and OHSS discussion is not very relevant to this low-response case.

Much of the advice is broadly IVF-consistent (single embryo transfer, cavity assessment with tubal factor/hydrosalpinx concern, cautious prognosis), but some recommendations are weakly supported or misplaced here, such as DAFI, donor-oocyte discussion at this stage, and OHSS/GnRH agonist emphasis in a low-yield cycle.

It offers some practical next steps—consider SET, assess uterine cavity/hydrosalpinx, review protocol, optimize lifestyle, discuss PGT-A cautiously—but recommendations are diffuse and not tightly prioritized for this specific transfer.
